status_summary: On 2025-03-24 Executive Order 14245 authorized the Secretary of State to impose a 25 percent tariff on countries importing Venezuelan oil, and Executive Order 14389 of 2026-02-20 ended those additional duties while leaving the underlying national emergency in effect; on 2025-11-16 the Secretary of State designated Cartel de los Soles a Foreign Terrorist Organization, effective on publication 2025-11-24. On 2026-01-03 US forces captured Nicolas Maduro and Cilia Flores in Caracas in an operation the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs described as military support for a law enforcement arrest on Southern District of New York narco-terrorism and cocaine importation charges, with Congress notified afterward; both pleaded not guilty at arraignment on 2026-01-05, and the former vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, was sworn in as interim president (USNI News, JURIST). Executive Order 14373 of 2026-01-09 declared a national emergency over the threat of judicial attachment of Venezuelan oil-sale funds held in Treasury accounts, directing that they be treated as Venezuelan sovereign property in US custody and disbursed only as the Secretary of State directs; OFAC issued General License 46 on 2026-01-29 for oil trade by established US companies (Mayer Brown), and the Embassy in Caracas formally reopened on 2026-03-30 after relations were restored in early March, with no election timetable announced (Algemeiner).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14245 was signed, authorizing a 25 percent tariff on goods from countries that import Venezuelan oil, at the Secretary of State's determination.
The Secretary of State signed the designation of Cartel de los Soles as a Foreign Terrorist Organization under INA section 219; it took effect on publication on 2025-11-24.

US forces captured Nicolas Maduro and Cilia Flores in Caracas (Operation Absolute Resolve) and flew them to New York to face Southern District of New York charges; officials described the operation as military support for a law enforcement arrest and notified Congress afterward.
Maduro and Flores were arraigned in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York and pleaded not guilty.

Executive Order 14373 (91 FR 2045) declared a national emergency over the threat of judicial attachment of Venezuelan government funds from oil and other natural resource sales held in designated Treasury accounts, barred judicial process against them, and directed Treasury to hold them as Venezuelan sovereign property and disburse them only as the Secretary of State directs.
OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 46 authorizing established US companies to trade in Venezuelan-origin oil under conditions, while keeping sanctions on the government and PDVSA.
Executive Order 14389 ended the additional IEEPA tariffs imposed under nine earlier orders, including EO 14245 on countries importing Venezuelan oil.
The State Department formally resumed operations at the US Embassy in Caracas, with diplomatic relations restored earlier in March.

title: Put the Maduro government on notice, contain Venezuela and unite the hemisphere against it
uncertainties: The record reads the Mandate text as a general posture; the capture of a sitting head of state and an interim arrangement with the former vice president go well beyond what the text names, so alignment is partial and progress is set mid-band. Executive Orders 14245, 14373 and 14389 and the Cartel de los Soles designation notice were read on federalregister.gov and govinfo.gov; Executive Order 14245 left the tariff to the Secretary of State's discretion, and no country-specific determination under it was verified. The capture, the stated legal basis and the arraignment rest on news reports (a naval affairs outlet and a legal news site), not on a Justice Department or State Department page; the operation name and the law enforcement framing are as reported there. The General License 46 date and terms come from a law firm summary, not the OFAC page. The embassy reopening rests on a news report quoting the State Department, whose site could not be reached. News leads (not opened) indicate Paraguay and Argentina designated Cartel de los Soles as a terrorist organization in August 2025, which bears on hemispheric alignment but is not a US action. Tren de Aragua designation, Operation Southern Spear boat strikes and humanitarian assistance were not separately sourced.
